items.title: Vulnerabilities and agency of small technologically advanced states: Finland navigating Sino-US strategic technology competition
items.evidence_note: Journal appears on the main Radar trusted-venue list; article-level peer review and claims require checking.
items.abstract_or_context: This article explores how a small technologically advanced state, exemplified by Finland, seeks to maintain agency and manage security risks in Sino-US strategic technology competition, and what future options experts envision for it. The US and China are presently the only ‘geoeconomic great powers’ with competences across four dimensions: investment leverage, supply chains, critical technologies, and technology standards. Given its close security ties to the United States, Finland is expected to align with it when faced with a choice between technological ecosystems.
